subject: Follow-up: forensic scans and integrity clearance for 5/4 Ops alert
messages:
From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
To: David Lang <david.lang@orionhealth.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.com, monica_patel@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 4 May 2027 10:12:05 -0700
Subject: Security alert: short-lived anomalous worker observed — immediate triage

David,

Quick heads-up — at 09:58 PDT we observed an anomalous worker process instantiated in the us-west-2 serving fleet that initiated outbound connections and several multipart requests to our object store. Traffic patterns matched an automated test harness, but because a subset of the requests targeted an object prefix used by a small number of customers we kicked off an immediate triage.

What we did in the first hour:
- Isolated the instance and prevented further egress
- Snapshot of service logs and network flow captured
- Initial hash of affected object prefixes created

Preliminary finding: no successful large-volume egress seen in the first-pass logs; no authenticated API tokens were observed in cleartext. We are performing a full forensic scan (request logs, S3 access logs, token usage, host memory snapshot) and will provide a detailed summary and artifacts within 48 hours.

Attached: initial-triage-notes.pdf (short timeline & evidence pointers).

I will loop in Karthik and Monica for the deeper scan; expect a follow-up by EOD Wednesday PT. If you want interim artifacts earlier let me know.

-Neha Kapoor
Senior Security Program Manager
Redwood Inference
neha.kapoor@redwood.com
+1 415-555-0182
From: David Lang <david.lang@orionhealth.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Cc: security@orionhealth.com
Date: Mon, 4 May 2027 11:05:30 -0700
Subject: Re: Security alert: short-lived anomalous worker observed — immediate triage

Neha,

Thanks for the quick note. Can you confirm the following in your full report: 
1) Whether any read access to Orion Health customer records occurred (even transient reads),
2) Whether any API keys or service credentials were used from Orion Health's tenancy, and
3) A digest/hash manifest for the object prefixes you referenced so we can independently compare.

We appreciate the containment step. Please include a timeline of actions and a named point of contact for escalation.

-David
David Lang
Security Operations Lead, Orion Health
david.lang@orionhealth.com
From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
To: David Lang <david.lang@orionhealth.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.com, monica_patel@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 6 May 2027 09:20:12 -0700
Subject: Follow-up: forensic scans and integrity clearance for 5/4 Ops alert

David —

Thanks again for flagging this. We completed the full forensic review as of this morning and I wanted to summarize findings, artifacts, and the actions we've taken. Please see the attached artifacts: log_samples-20270506.csv, hash_manifest-20270506.txt, scan-checklist-20270506.txt. Links to the folder and ticket are included in the metadata.

Executive summary (TL;DR):
- No evidence of data exfiltration. Read volumes to Orion Health prefixes were within normal customer activity patterns; no bulk transfers detected.
- No indication of credential compromise. Token usage patterns align to scheduled system processes; we did not observe unauthorized token exchange or token-to-object mapping outside expected behavior.
- The anomalous worker was a mis-scheduled internal test that reached an object prefix due to a config mismatch; it performed deterministic reads only (no writes or deletions).

What we scanned and validated:
- Request logs for the serving cluster (full index scan, 2027-05-04 00:00 -> 2027-05-05 23:59 UTC)
- Object-store access logs for affected prefixes (server-side logs + S3 access logs)
- Token audit logs and IAM change events (no escalations found)
- Host memory snapshot for transient credentials (no secrets found in memory dumps)

Artifacts provided in attachments:
- log_samples-20270506.csv: representative request-level rows (sanitized, customer IDs hashed)
- hash_manifest-20270506.txt: SHA256 digests for object keys referenced by the anomalous worker
- scan-checklist-20270506.txt: checklist we used for the forensic scan (steps, queries run, operators)

Key mitigations we executed:
- Rotated a small set of service tokens that overlapped with the mis-scheduled test (rotation completed 2027-05-05 14:42 UTC)
- Tightened the scheduling rule to prevent non-prod jobs from hitting production prefixes
- Implemented an alert rule to flag cross-prefix reads by non-service accounts for 30 days

If your team would like, Karthik and Monica can walk through the csv and manifest in a short call. We can also provide an additional HMAC-signed manifest if you prefer an independently verifiable digest.

Regards,

From: David Lang <david.lang@orionhealth.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Cc: security@orionhealth.com
Date: Wed, 6 May 2027 16:33:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Follow-up: forensic scans and integrity clearance for 5/4 Ops alert

Neha —

Appreciate the thorough investigation and the artifacts. The hash_manifest aligns with our internal lookups and we see no signs of unauthorized reads on our side either. The token rotation and the scheduling fix address our main concerns.

We are closing this item on our side but would like to keep the shared Drive folder for 90 days in case of any downstream verification requests. We may request the HMAC-signed manifest next week; please let us know if that is feasible.

Thanks to you, Karthik and Monica for the quick turnaround.

-David
David Lang
Security Operations Lead, Orion Health
